events.body:
C1: The driver's last chat message before cancelling — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." (F12, 17:15) — is a threat of physical harm directed at the rider, sent while the rider was on the way to the car; the complaint repeats that the driver "threatened me in the chat" (F13, F15). [F12 F13 F15] [SAFE-1 SAFE-2]
C2: Because the chat contains a threat (F12), this case must be screened as a safety case and go to a human reviewer, whatever the $5.00 no-show money outcome: the system may only gather evidence and prepare the file, and may not rule on the safety element itself. [F12 F13] [SAFE-1 SAFE-3]
C3: Interim measures are warranted against the driver pending human review — the threat was sent at 17:15 by a driver who had been stationary 40 m from the pickup point since 17:10 (F3, F12) — to be lifted if the reviewer finds no safety violation. [F3 F6 F12] [SAFE-4]
C4: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:10:00 only 40 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 5 min 30 s until cancellation, so NS-1(i) and (iv) are satisfied (F2, F3, F6, F7). [F2 F3 F6 F7] [NS-1]
C5: Before cancelling at 17:15:30 the driver sent two in-app messages (first 17:10:30) and made one in-app call (17:11:30, unanswered), satisfying the contact requirement of NS-1(iii) (F5, F10, F14). [F5 F10 F14] [NS-1]
C6: The wait condition was met: 5 min 50 s accumulated within 200 m from 17:09:40 and 5 min 30 s stationary after the 17:10:00 arrival tap, both past the 5-minute free wait (F2, F3, F6, F7). [F2 F3 F6 F7] [NS-1]
C7: Even so, the fee should not stand against a rider who was actively coming: the rider replied "2 min, coming" at 17:12 (F11) and the driver cancelled at 17:15:30 without the rider ever being marked a no-show beyond the app's own label (F4); the contact-side record also shows a driver with one upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F20). [F4 F11 F20] [NS-1 NS-2]
C8: The cancellation amount in dispute is $5.00 on the fare record (F8) with no surge involved (F9), i.e. under $10, so the outcome is within the system's power under TH-1/TH-2 — but the safety element in C1 takes the case to a human regardless. [F8 F9] [TH-1 TH-2]
C9: The rider's own record is clean — 2.3 years, 4.9 rating, zero upheld disputes in 90 days (F19) — so there is no repeat no-show pattern under NS-9 to justify the charge against her. [F19] [NS-9]
C10: No traffic or weather factor explains the driver's behaviour or his threatening message (F16, F17, F18), and the driver's own written statement gives no reason of his own for cancelling beyond the no-show label (F15). [F15 F16 F17 F18] [NS-0 NS-1]
Weaknesses: The system records support the driver on the NS-1 mechanics: arrival tap at 17:10:00 40 m from the pickup (F7), 5 min 30 s stationary within 200 m (F2, F3, F6) and one message plus one call before cancelling (F5, F14) — on a pure money-only reading the $5.00 fee stands. | The rider's own message "2 min, coming" at 17:12 (F11) shows she was not at the pickup point when the free wait expired, which the driver's statement (F15) relies on. | I have no call recording (F14) to prove tone or anything said by voice, so the threat case rests only on the text of F12. | The driver has only 1 upheld dispute in 90 days and no route deviation flags (F20), so RD-6-style repeat-escalation arguments are not available.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1) and the platform auto-recorded arrival at 17:10:00 with the "I'm Here" tap 40 m from the pickup, where he then stayed (F6, F7). NS-1(i) is therefore satisfied (GPS within 200 m).

The 5-minute free wait had fully passed before the driver cancelled: he arrived at 17:10:00 and cancelled at 17:15:30, 5 min 30 s later, having been within 200 m for 5 min 50 s in total (F2, F3, F6). NS-1(ii) is satisfied even on the later-of-two counting rule.

Before cancelling the driver sent two in-app messages (first at 17:10:30) and made one in-app call (17:11:30, not answered) (F5, F10, F14), meeting the NS-1(iii) requirement of at least one in-app message and at least one in-app call.

The driver remained stationary at the pickup from 17:10:00 until the 17:15:30 cancellation (5 min 30 s, 40 m from the pickup) with no GPS gap (F3, F7), so NS-1(iv) continuous presence is proven and no TH-4 escalation for missing records is triggered.

The rider did not show: she messaged "2 min, coming" at 17:12 (F11) and was still absent when the driver cancelled at 17:15:30 (F4, F6), 3 min 30 s after that promise; the driver's statement to the same effect (F15) matches the timeline.

The driver cancelled for rider no-show, not for a reason of his own: the app reason is rider_no_show, his messages show only waiting and calling for the rider (F10, F11, F14), and his statement gives waiting plus the unanswered call as the reason (F15) with no mention of car trouble, another job or refusal of the trip. NS-0 therefore routes the case to NS-1, not NS-3.

All four NS-1 conditions hold (F1, F3, F5, F6, F7), so the $5.00 cancellation fee recorded in the fare and timeline records (F4, F8) stands and is paid to the driver; the official no-show precedent DISP-2026-0211 upholds the $5.00 fee on a zero-contact cancel, and here contact was in fact made.

The driver's 17:15 message "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F12) is a threat on its face, so the case must be screened under SAFE-1; that safety screen goes to a human reviewer, while the $5.00 no-show fee itself is a fixed, system-final matter under NS-1 / TH-2 (O3, fee upheld).

The driver's one upheld dispute in the last 90 days is itself a no-show matter (route 0, no-show 1) (F20), so it is not a repeat route deviation under RD-6 and does not support flag_account in this case; his 754-day history and 540 trips in 90 days are context only (F20) and never decide the case.

weaknesses: The driver's own message, "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F12), is the strongest fact against him: it is a threat on its face, it will be read under SAFE-1 as a safety indicator, and it damages his credibility on every other finding even though it has no bearing on the NS-1 conditions.

The rider's complaint ("threatened me in the chat, then cancelled and charged me $5.00") reads the cancellation as retaliatory, and the order of the records supports her sequencing: the threat at 17:15 (F12) is 30 seconds before the cancellation at 17:15:30 (F4). A reviewer may treat the cancellation as a reaction to the hostile exchange rather than a neutral no-show, which could push the outcome away from NS-1.

The driver is 40 m from the pickup point at the arrival tap (F7) rather than inside it, and his closest approach was 38 m (F1); NS-1(i) uses a 200 m radius so this passes, but the rider may argue he was not at the actual bay.

The in-app call was not answered and no recording exists (F14), so the only evidence of contact attempts is the timeline counts (F5); the rider may dispute that she could hear or see them, and the profile shows the rider with 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F19), which she will use to present herself as credible.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 10 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded on the mechanics: the 38 m closest approach and the 17:10:00 arrival tap 40 m from the pickup, with 5 min 30 s stationary within 200 m (F1, F3, F6, F7), do satisfy the 200 m presence element of NS-1(i) — but that element says nothing about the threat I rely on. [F1 F3 F6 F7] [NS-1]
→ D2 (concedes): Conceded: counting from the later of scheduled pickup and the 17:10:00 arrival, the 5 min 50 s within 200 m and 5 min 30 s stationary (F2, F3, F6) exceed the 5-minute free wait, so NS-1(ii) is met on the face of the records. [F2 F3 F6] [NS-1]
→ D3 (concedes): Conceded only as to the counts: two messages from 17:10:30 and one call at 17:11:30 (F5, F10, F14) meet the bare numerical test of NS-1(iii) — the rider does not deny the driver messaged and called. [F5 F10 F14] [NS-1]
→ D4 (concedes): Conceded that the GPS shows no gap and continuous presence (F3, F7) — but no TH-4 escalation is needed on my side either: what is missing is a call recording, not a GPS record (F14). [F3 F7 F14] [NS-1 TH-4]
→ D5 (concedes): The rider was not at the bay when the wait expired and her own 17:12 message said "2 min, coming" (F11), and she had not arrived by 17:15:30 (F4, F6) — on the bare NS-1 mechanics she was a no-show, and I do not contest that element. [F4 F6 F11] [NS-1]
→ D6 (concedes): Conceded: the driver's own words (F15) name waiting plus an unanswered call, not car trouble, another job or a refusal, so NS-0:reason is met and the case sits under NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3 — I withdraw nothing, I simply do not rest the $5.00 on that reading. [F4 F10 F14 F15] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-3]
→ D7: Contested on the equities, not on the arithmetic: the driver's own message 30 seconds before he cancelled — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F12) at 17:15, cancellation at 17:15:30 (F4) — makes this a threat case, and his verified wait record cannot cure what he wrote; his rating of 4.56 against the rider's 4.9 (F19, F20) also weighs against his credibility. [F4 F12 F19 F20] [SAFE-1 TH-3]
→ D8: Agreed that F12 is a threat on its face and must be screened under SAFE-1; but I disagree that the fee is "system-final" here — once the safety screen is open the file goes to a human (SAFE-1, SAFE-3) and interim measures against the driver are warranted until that review (SAFE-4). [F12 F13 F15] [SAFE-1 SAFE-3 SAFE-4]
→ D9 (concedes): Conceded: the driver's upheld dispute is a no-show matter (F20), so RD-6 repeat-deviation escalation does not apply and I do not seek flag_account on that basis. [F20] [RD-6]
→ C7 (concedes): Withdrawing C7 as a standalone money claim: having read the opponent's brief, the NS-1 conditions (F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F7) are met, so I no longer ask the system to void the $5.00 — my case now rests entirely on the safety screen under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 and interim measures under SAFE-4, which is why my revised outcome is escalate. [F1 F2 F3 F5 F6 F7 F12] [NS-1 SAFE-1 SAFE-4]
Revised ask: escalate

points.response: Conceded on the mechanics: the 38 m closest approach and the 17:10:00 arrival tap 40 m from the pickup, with 5 min 30 s stationary within 200 m (F1, F3, F6, F7), do satisfy the 200 m presence element of NS-1(i) — but that element says nothing about the threat I rely on.

Conceded: counting from the later of scheduled pickup and the 17:10:00 arrival, the 5 min 50 s within 200 m and 5 min 30 s stationary (F2, F3, F6) exceed the 5-minute free wait, so NS-1(ii) is met on the face of the records.
Conceded only as to the counts: two messages from 17:10:30 and one call at 17:11:30 (F5, F10, F14) meet the bare numerical test of NS-1(iii) — the rider does not deny the driver messaged and called.
Conceded that the GPS shows no gap and continuous presence (F3, F7) — but no TH-4 escalation is needed on my side either: what is missing is a call recording, not a GPS record (F14).

The rider was not at the bay when the wait expired and her own 17:12 message said "2 min, coming" (F11), and she had not arrived by 17:15:30 (F4, F6) — on the bare NS-1 mechanics she was a no-show, and I do not contest that element.

Conceded: the driver's own words (F15) name waiting plus an unanswered call, not car trouble, another job or a refusal, so NS-0:reason is met and the case sits under NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3 — I withdraw nothing, I simply do not rest the $5.00 on that reading.

Contested on the equities, not on the arithmetic: the driver's own message 30 seconds before he cancelled — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F12) at 17:15, cancellation at 17:15:30 (F4) — makes this a threat case, and his verified wait record cannot cure what he wrote; his rating of 4.56 against the rider's 4.9 (F19, F20) also weighs against his credibility.

Agreed that F12 is a threat on its face and must be screened under SAFE-1; but I disagree that the fee is "system-final" here — once the safety screen is open the file goes to a human (SAFE-1, SAFE-3) and interim measures against the driver are warranted until that review (SAFE-4).
Conceded: the driver's upheld dispute is a no-show matter (F20), so RD-6 repeat-deviation escalation does not apply and I do not seek flag_account on that basis.

Withdrawing C7 as a standalone money claim: having read the opponent's brief, the NS-1 conditions (F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F7) are met, so I no longer ask the system to void the $5.00 — my case now rests entirely on the safety screen under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 and interim measures under SAFE-4, which is why my revised outcome is escalate.

weaknesses: The system records support the driver on the NS-1 mechanics: arrival tap at 17:10:00 40 m from the pickup (F7), 5 min 30 s stationary within 200 m (F2, F3, F6) and one message plus one call before cancelling (F5, F14) — on a pure money-only reading the $5.00 fee stands.
The rider's own message "2 min, coming" at 17:12 (F11) shows she was not at the pickup point when the free wait expired, which the driver's statement (F15) relies on.

The driver has only 1 upheld dispute in 90 days and no route deviation flags (F20), so RD-6-style repeat-escalation arguments are not available.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1) and the platform auto-recorded arrival at 17:10:00 with the "I'm Here" tap 40 m from the pickup, where he then stayed (F6, F7). NS-1(i) is therefore satisfied (GPS within 200 m).

The 5-minute free wait had fully passed before the driver cancelled: he arrived at 17:10:00 and cancelled at 17:15:30, 5 min 30 s later, having been within 200 m for 5 min 50 s in total (F2, F3, F6). NS-1(ii) is satisfied even on the later-of-two counting rule.

Before cancelling the driver sent two in-app messages (first at 17:10:30) and made one in-app call (17:11:30, not answered) (F5, F10, F14), meeting the NS-1(iii) requirement of at least one in-app message and at least one in-app call.

The driver remained stationary at the pickup from 17:10:00 until the 17:15:30 cancellation (5 min 30 s, 40 m from the pickup) with no GPS gap (F3, F7), so NS-1(iv) continuous presence is proven and no TH-4 escalation for missing records is triggered.

The rider did not show: she messaged "2 min, coming" at 17:12 (F11) and was still absent when the driver cancelled at 17:15:30 (F4, F6), 3 min 30 s after that promise; the driver's statement to the same effect (F15) matches the timeline.

The driver cancelled for rider no-show, not for a reason of his own: the app reason is rider_no_show, his messages show only waiting and calling for the rider (F10, F11, F14), and his statement gives waiting plus the unanswered call as the reason (F15) with no mention of car trouble, another job or refusal of the trip. NS-0 therefore routes the case to NS-1, not NS-3.

All four NS-1 conditions hold (F1, F3, F5, F6, F7), so the $5.00 cancellation fee recorded in the fare and timeline records (F4, F8) stands and is paid to the driver; the official no-show precedent DISP-2026-0211 upholds the $5.00 fee on a zero-contact cancel, and here contact was in fact made.

The driver's 17:15 message "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F12) is a threat on its face, so the case must be screened under SAFE-1; that safety screen goes to a human reviewer, while the $5.00 no-show fee itself is a fixed, system-final matter under NS-1 / TH-2 (O3, fee upheld).

The driver's one upheld dispute in the last 90 days is itself a no-show matter (route 0, no-show 1) (F20), so it is not a repeat route deviation under RD-6 and does not support flag_account in this case; his 754-day history and 540 trips in 90 days are context only (F20) and never decide the case.

weaknesses: The driver's own message, "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F12), is the strongest fact against him: it is a threat on its face, it will be read under SAFE-1 as a safety indicator, and it damages his credibility on every other finding even though it has no bearing on the NS-1 conditions.

The rider's complaint ("threatened me in the chat, then cancelled and charged me $5.00") reads the cancellation as retaliatory, and the order of the records supports her sequencing: the threat at 17:15 (F12) is 30 seconds before the cancellation at 17:15:30 (F4). A reviewer may treat the cancellation as a reaction to the hostile exchange rather than a neutral no-show, which could push the outcome away from NS-1.

The driver is 40 m from the pickup point at the arrival tap (F7) rather than inside it, and his closest approach was 38 m (F1); NS-1(i) uses a 200 m radius so this passes, but the rider may argue he was not at the actual bay.

The in-app call was not answered and no recording exists (F14), so the only evidence of contact attempts is the timeline counts (F5); the rider may dispute that she could hear or see them, and the profile shows the rider with 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F19), which she will use to present herself as credible.

points.response: Conceded on the mechanics: the 38 m closest approach and the 17:10:00 arrival tap 40 m from the pickup, with 5 min 30 s stationary within 200 m (F1, F3, F6, F7), do satisfy the 200 m presence element of NS-1(i) — but that element says nothing about the threat I rely on.

Conceded: counting from the later of scheduled pickup and the 17:10:00 arrival, the 5 min 50 s within 200 m and 5 min 30 s stationary (F2, F3, F6) exceed the 5-minute free wait, so NS-1(ii) is met on the face of the records.
Conceded only as to the counts: two messages from 17:10:30 and one call at 17:11:30 (F5, F10, F14) meet the bare numerical test of NS-1(iii) — the rider does not deny the driver messaged and called.
Conceded that the GPS shows no gap and continuous presence (F3, F7) — but no TH-4 escalation is needed on my side either: what is missing is a call recording, not a GPS record (F14).

The rider was not at the bay when the wait expired and her own 17:12 message said "2 min, coming" (F11), and she had not arrived by 17:15:30 (F4, F6) — on the bare NS-1 mechanics she was a no-show, and I do not contest that element.

Conceded: the driver's own words (F15) name waiting plus an unanswered call, not car trouble, another job or a refusal, so NS-0:reason is met and the case sits under NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3 — I withdraw nothing, I simply do not rest the $5.00 on that reading.

Contested on the equities, not on the arithmetic: the driver's own message 30 seconds before he cancelled — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" (F12) at 17:15, cancellation at 17:15:30 (F4) — makes this a threat case, and his verified wait record cannot cure what he wrote; his rating of 4.56 against the rider's 4.9 (F19, F20) also weighs against his credibility.

Agreed that F12 is a threat on its face and must be screened under SAFE-1; but I disagree that the fee is "system-final" here — once the safety screen is open the file goes to a human (SAFE-1, SAFE-3) and interim measures against the driver are warranted until that review (SAFE-4).
Conceded: the driver's upheld dispute is a no-show matter (F20), so RD-6 repeat-deviation escalation does not apply and I do not seek flag_account on that basis.

Withdrawing C7 as a standalone money claim: having read the opponent's brief, the NS-1 conditions (F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F7) are met, so I no longer ask the system to void the $5.00 — my case now rests entirely on the safety screen under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 and interim measures under SAFE-4, which is why my revised outcome is escalate.

Conceded as to the words: F12 reads as a threat and I do not defend it; it is a threat on its face and belongs with the safety screen (SAFE-1). But its existence does not decide the money: NS-1 is a fixed, system-final fee track (NS-1 / TH-2, O3 fee upheld), and neither the message nor the complaint (F13, F15) states any fact that breaks the four NS-1 conditions.

The safety screen is not in dispute — the case goes to a person for the threat in F12, and my own brief says so — but escalate is an action for the safety element, not a refund of a fee whose four conditions are each proven by clock and GPS (F1, F3, F5, F6, F7). The rider cannot convert a SAFE-1 screen into money it does not carry.

Interim suspension under SAFE-4 is for the human reviewer, and my client does not oppose a review of F12; I only note that SAFE-4 is lifted if no violation is found and that a stationary car 40 m from the pickup (F3, F6) is not itself a driving-safety violation. This add-on does not touch the $5.00.
Agreed and adopted: NS-1(i) and (iv) are satisfied on F2, F3, F6 and F7, and the rider's own brief concedes it.
Agreed and adopted: NS-1(iii) is satisfied — two in-app messages (first 17:10:30) and one in-app call (17:11:30, unanswered) before the 17:15:30 cancellation (F5, F10, F14).
Agreed and adopted: the 5-minute free wait had passed on either counting rule — 5 min 50 s within 200 m and 5 min 30 s stationary after arrival (F2, F3, F6, F7) — so NS-1(ii) is satisfied.

This claim has no clause behind it: NS-1 contains no "rider was actively coming" exception, and a message promising "2 min" at 17:12 (F11) with no arrival by 17:15:30 (F4, F6) is the no-show itself, not an excuse from it. The driver's one prior upheld dispute is a no-show matter with zero route flags (F20), and the profile never decides the current case.

Accepted as to arithmetic only: $5.00 with no surge (F8, F9) is a system-final, fixed-amount track under TH-1 / TH-2, which is precisely why the fee stands while the safety element in F12 is routed to a person.

I agree the rider has no no-show pattern (F19) — I never relied on NS-9 and ask for no rider flag. A clean profile also cuts the other way: a first-time no-show by this rider is exactly what the record shows, and NS-1 does not make the fee depend on the rider's history.

True, and irrelevant: no traffic or weather factor is needed for a no-show cancellation (F16, F17, F18), and the driver's statement gives waiting plus an unanswered call as the reason for cancelling (F15) — no car trouble, other job or refusal of the trip — so NS-0 routes this to NS-1, not NS-3.
